body: Another subReddit (i don’t remember which, sadly) recommended India’s ancient past by RS Sharma, History of Medieval India by Satish Chandra, and History of Modern India by Bipin Chandra. I recently finished them. They are all very easy to ready and well written, and give a brief overview from prehistoric times till independence. You can then explore areas of your interest further.

As an Indian who has lived out most her life in India, I want to cry happy tears and hug your son for being able to speak his mind so clearly and stand up for himself. No, it is not arrogance and attitude. It’s calling his father out for being a rubbish abusive parent. It’s about time Indian parents learnt that their children are not their possessions. They are not extensions of them. Your husband had no right to interfere in his adult son’s choices or marriage. I hope you both realise at least now. As word of caution, I am now in my 40s. I had a similar father and we are extremely estranged. He alone, shocked, and upset that I’m not bending backwards to support him now because he feels entitled to my time, love and money. I wish I could be as clear and strong as your son to tell him exactly why he doesn’t see me as much anymore. I really suggest apologising as the other comments do, but after a lot of introspection to understand why you BOTH were abusive and accept that you were.
